Dev Engineer Review

  • Reuses ALL_REUSABLE V2 decode KV cache across turns.
  • Commits only the stable generation prefix after sampling state and speculative KV relocation.
  • Excludes the newest sampled token until its KV is materialized.
  • Preserves prompt-only reuse for draft caches and compression-managed history.
  • Uses zero-copy token views and materializes only newly committed tokens.
  • Prevents duplicate resource updates by skipping only the target V2 KV cache manager.
  • No public API declarations changed. The ResourceManager.update_resources signature gained an optional parameter with a default value, which preserves existing callers.
  • No configuration files or test-list files changed.
  • Runtime and error-handling regressions require validation through the listed tests and integration results.

QA Engineer Review

Modified test files:

  • tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_compression_manager.py
    • Updated resource-manager relocation expectations.
    • Added coverage for include_finished_requests=True.
    • Added coverage that skipping the target KV cache manager still updates draft and compression managers.
  • tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py
    • Added zero-copy token retrieval and Python-backend materialization coverage.
    • Added commit-boundary coverage for context-only requests, normal generation, compression-managed history, completed generation, partial materialized prefixes, empty final commits, and guard conditions.
  • tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_v2_capacity_only.py
    • Added test_generation_commit_runs_after_stable_history_resize.
    • Added test_finished_spec_request_relocates_before_resize_and_commit.

No modified test functions were reported as covered in tests/integration/test_lists/. The changes provide focused unit coverage for commit boundaries, speculative relocation, token slicing, resource-manager behavior, and the TriAttention guard.

Verdict: sufficient.

Description

KVCacheManagerV2 stopped committing after prefill, so generation KV produced by decode was not retained in the reusable block index. For a multi-turn disaggregated request, the decode worker could reuse the original prompt but had to receive the previous turn's output KV again.

This change keeps ALL_REUSABLE V2 caches open after prefill and commits only the stable generation prefix after sampling state is applied and before response handling can remove the request. The newest sampled token is excluded because its KV is not materialized until the next forward pass. Accepted speculative KV relocation and history resize complete before commit. Generation commit remains disabled for draft caches and compression that manages physical history, preserving prompt-only reuse for TriAttention. Token collection uses a zero-copy view and materializes only the newly committed slice, avoiding an O(sequence length) Python-list conversion on every decode step.

The generic resource-manager update skips only the target V2 KV manager to avoid updating it twice while preserving draft KV and KV compression manager updates. This change does not modify the transfer-side prefix trimming algorithm or any public API.

Test Coverage

  • Focused unit tests cover context/decode commit boundaries, terminal commit, speculative-KV relocation, Python token slicing, target-only resource-manager skipping, and the TriAttention generation-commit guard.
  • B200 1P1D with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, NIXL, 32-token blocks, and both scheduler modes: the matched second-turn transfer decreased from 3 blocks to 1 block, initial/forced-miss transfers remained 5/7 blocks, and outputs were token-identical to baseline.
  • B200 1P1D with one-model EAGLE3, using both linear and dynamic-tree decoding: transfers changed from 5/3/7 to 5/1/7 blocks and all outputs matched baseline.

Estimated code review effort: 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes

Merge Risk: 🔵 Low · up to 2d15a

This change enables reusable decode KV prefixes across turns, but same-pass cancellations in PP and non-overlap execution may leave a reusable cache commit unfinalized. Reorder cancellation handling before V2 generation-resource updates to make terminal cache state consistent.

  participant KVCacheManagerV2

  KVCacheManagerV2->>KVCacheManagerV2: relocate finished draft tokens and resize cache
  KVCacheManagerV2->>KVCacheManagerV2: commit generation blocks
  PyExecutor->>ResourceManager: update shared resources with KV manager skipped

Run _handle_canceled_requests() before _update_v2_generation_resources() in the PP and non-overlap paths. The overlap path already uses this order. A same-pass cancellation otherwise leaves request.state non-terminal when try_commit_generation_blocks() computes is_end, so it records False. _KVCache.close() can commit a partial attention block, but it does not replace the terminal SSM handling associated with is_end=True.

One beam-search edge case: the generation commit size is derived from request.max_beam_num_tokens, but _reuse_token_source() always returns beam 0. Once beams diverge, the longest beam can be ahead of beam 0, so stable_token_count can ask the cache to commit beyond beam 0's actual stable history. Could generation reuse be disabled for beam width > 1, or compute the commit boundary from the same beam whose tokens are committed?
